item.title: An Afternoon at the Clock Shop
item.summary: A shop assistant talks about learning to listen to old clocks.
item.content_markdown:
**Reporter:** When did you start working here?

**Elina:** Last summer. At first I cleaned the glass on the clocks and put labels next to them. My uncle repairs the clocks. He said I could help with repairs later, after I had learned how to listen to the different sounds.

**Reporter:** What did you listen for?

**Elina:** He put two clocks on the same shelf. One made a regular sound: tick, tick, tick. The other went quiet for a moment between some of its ticks. I listened again with my eyes closed. Then I could tell which clock was the second one without seeing it.

**Reporter:** Do you work on clocks by yourself now?

**Elina:** Only on small jobs. Today I put a new glass cover on a clock. When I cannot find the cause of a problem, I write down what I heard or saw. My uncle reads my notes before he opens the clock. He says the notes help us remember what it was doing when it came in.
